newsitem.title: USA: GKN bid for Sinter should succeed - arbs.
newsitem.headline: GKN bid for Sinter should succeed - arbs.

text.p: Britain's GKN Plc is offering a fair price for Cleveland-based auto parts maker Sinter Metals Inc and the deal is expected to close as planned, Wall Street arbitragers said.
Arbitragers said they expect the approval of a 43 percent shareholder in Sinter to ensure the proposed transaction, which was announced by GKN earlier Wednesday.
"This deal looks very plain vanilla. GKN is a huge company and they have the money to buy Sinter, one of the premier makers of auto parts," said an arb, who declined to be identified.
Shares in Cleveland-based Sinter soared toward the $37 offered by GKN in heavy trade Wednesday, rising 9-5/8 to 36-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange trade.

"It obviously is a friendly deal," said the arb. He said it is unclear whether there could have been any dissent on the Sinter board because the company provided no information on its directors' vote. Sinter spokesman would not comment on the board vote.
"Sinter was not shopped around, but at 8.1 times cash flow, the price is in line with the multiple being paid for companies like this," the arb said.
The 43 percent stake backing the deal is held primarily by Sinter chairman Joseph Carreras and Citicorp's Citicorp Venture Capital Ltd, a Sinter spokesman said.
A second arbitrager noted the fullness of the price, saying, "Citicorp Venture Capital is not the type to let their stock go cheaply."
